status: PROPOSAL ONLY: additional exact process.env interceptor integrity prerequisite

v8.name: JSObject::PreventExtensions
PreventExtensionsWithTransition

findings: Actual Node CreateEnvProxyTemplate installs a named interceptor. Original V8 PreventExtensions and PreventExtensionsWithTransition explicitly refuse named/indexed interceptors; the latter chooses the distinct prevent/seal/freeze failure at that point before property enumeration.

Current QuickJS JS_PreventExtensions only delegates for Proxy, rejects selected RAB cases, then clears extensible for an ordinary custom class. The existing exotic-method ABI has no matching prevention callback.

Therefore a custom process.env class built solely from current getter/query/setter/delete/enumerate/define hooks would incorrectly become non-extensible. Object.seal/freeze could then enumerate and call its definer after mutating extensibility, unlike the original early rejection.

Current QuickJS Object.preventExtensions converts a false raw result to its TypeError while Reflect.preventExtensions returns false. Current seal/freeze uses the same raw helper, but its existing false case has a Proxy-specific diagnostic. A complete selected adaptation must preserve the separate original modes without altering absent-hook/Proxy behavior.
proposed_boundary: Have VM evaluate a narrow opt-in exotic prevention capability for the actual interceptor class, keeping the previous path byte-identical when absent.
The operation must refuse without mutating extensibility or enumerating/getting/defining properties. Reflect's false result and the actual Object prevent/seal/freeze throw modes must remain distinct.

A raw-false-only hook would fix state mutation but leave seal/freeze diagnostic selection incomplete. The final VM design should state the mode/diagnostic cutpoint rather than manufacture guest property probes.

Own causal controls must check unchanged extensibility, zero query/get/enumeration/define observations, correct separate Object/Reflect outcomes, and unchanged ordinary/Proxy behavior. This packet authorizes neither C edits nor execution.
